script.spoken: Why a repeat of 1859 could cost $2.6 trillion. The 1859 Carrington storm set telegraph stations on fire. Telegraph systems across Europe and North America failed. Some operators even got electric shocks. In 2012, a similar storm missed Earth by about 9 days. A 2013 estimate put a repeat's U.S. cost at $600 billion to $2.6 trillion. Today, long power lines and satellites would take the hit. So the same storm would cost far more now than then.
